issues.legal_issue: In a case based on circumstantial evidence, the prosecution must establish every circumstance and a complete chain that proves guilt beyond reasonable doubt and excludes every reasonable hypothesis consistent with innocence.
Whether the evidence established the alleged motive, last-seen circumstance, and recoveries of incriminating articles sufficiently to prove the accused’s guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
Whether the alleged weapon recoveries could support the prosecution case when the recovery evidence was not properly proved and the forensic report did not establish the blood group.
Whether the conviction and death sentence could be sustained when the prosecution failed to prove the incriminating circumstances and the lower courts overlooked material infirmities in the evidence.
